- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 75+), then fails to correct downward in subsequent days.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing true price trends — especially when true values rise sharply, model takes 2–3 days to adjust.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior averages too quickly, underestimating sustained upward trends.
- Overconfident in short-term volatility — forecasts often peak too early and then drop too fast, missing sustained momentum.
- When true prices are rising steadily, model underestimates the rate of increase, especially in the last 10–15 days of the forecast.
- Model tends to underestimate the impact of policy or market events that cause sudden price jumps — often misses the “trigger” and reacts too slowly.
